title: fix: use typesafe/jev-1.13 as the canonical model name
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Names the public model `typesafe/jev-1.13`, matching the existing upstream version; preserves `jev` and `typesafe/jev` as aliases.
- Updates the decisions default, Ask Jev client, source docs, and pricing snapshot key. Pricing and upstream routing stay the same.
- Verifies existing API keys restricted to `typesafe/jev` can use the canonical name and both aliases.
- Validation: 48 gateway tests, 9 Ask Jev tests, gateway typecheck, and Biome pass.

gist.headline: Jev got its full name
gist.blurb: Jev’s proper upstream name is now the one on the label: `typesafe/jev-1.13`. The old nicknames still answer when called, because migrations should not require interpretive dance.
gist.summary: The public Jev model is now canonically named `typesafe/jev-1.13`, matching its upstream version, while `jev` and `typesafe/jev` remain supported aliases across routing, pricing, docs, decisions, and Ask Jev.
gist.impact: Developers can use `typesafe/jev-1.13` in API requests—including with keys previously restricted to `typesafe/jev`—while existing requests using either alias continue to work with unchanged pricing and upstream routing.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy model-name garden where three plant labels—`typesafe/jev-1.13`, `typesafe/jev`, and `jev`—point to the same healthy code-flower. Polli, wearing tiny librarian glasses, carefully replaces the main label while a friendly CRT monitor robot confirms all three paths lead to the same bloom.
